claims.statement: MinIO storage fields include service URL with illustrative port 9000, S3 bucket and MINIO_ACCESS_KEY/MINIO_SECRET_KEY values. Field names and placeholders are not real credentials or authorized configuration.

GHES Actions is designed for environments lacking full internet access; by default workflows cannot use dotcom/Marketplace actions. Offline design is not proof all dependencies work without network preparation.

When storage authentication uses OIDC, instance token discovery and JWKS URLs under /_services/token/.well-known/openid-configuration and /_services/token/.well-known/jwks must be publicly reachable for the provider. This conditional exposure requirement is not authorization to publish endpoints or the whole instance.

Successful configuration run enables Actions; subsequent access-policy and self-hosted-runner setup is separately linked. Source expectation does not prove successful installation, readiness or native enforcement.

Bucket access-key permissions include s3:PutObject, GetObject, ListBucketMultipartUploads, ListMultipartUploadParts, AbortMultipartUpload, DeleteObject and ListBucket; destructive object access is a described requirement, not an actual granted permission.
kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt are additional permissions only when KMS encryption is enabled; do not require unconditional KMS grants or infer encryption configured.
S3 setup fields specify regional service URL (us-west-2 example), bucket and access-key ID/secret; endpoint documentation is separately linked. No credential fetched, persisted or created.
Enterprise artifact/log setup selects Amazon S3 Setup; the UI step does not establish authorized storage, correct credentials or successful writes.

Other S3-compatible GHES storage products are partner self-validated; Technology Partnership providers own support/documentation. Self-validation and linked partner inventory are not an independent compatibility certificate.

Trusted-authority TLS is strongly recommended for GHES. Self-signed certificates can work with extra self-hosted-runner configuration but are not recommended for production; this is not an absolute impossibility claim.
GHES self-hosted setup actions may need a prepared tools cache when runners lack internet. Conditional source scope and linked preparation remain distinct from observed cache completeness.

GHES external storage authentication may use OIDC or traditional secrets; OIDC is recommended where possible to avoid managing long-lived secrets. After trust setup, provider short-lived tokens expire automatically; trust, availability and privilege scope are not certified here.
External Actions storage overview includes a shared storage-contents fragment and links external requirements; standalone reference does not establish reviewed requirements or working provider setup.
External blob storage holds workflow-generated logs, caches and user-uploaded build artifacts; storage category is not an assurance of retention, integrity or recovery.

GHES backup and high-availability configurations do not protect external Actions artifacts/logs; data protection and replication depend on the external provider. Provider choice alone is not proof of configured backups or tested restoration.

Managed users lack hosted-runner entitlement minutes; the source suggests fork and pull request into an organization for nonmember contributions, running workflows on organization runners. This does not override actual fork, PR approval or runner-access policy.

An environment-referencing job creates a deployment with environment name and status records carrying environment, optional environment_url and job state. These records do not alone prove real deployment success or required protection checks.

Default GITHUB_* and RUNNER_* environment values cannot be overwritten. CI may currently be overwritten but future support is not guaranteed; pinned behavior is not permission to falsify runtime identity.
Treat environment variables as case sensitive as a portability practice regardless of OS/shell behavior; recommendation is separate from actual case semantics.
An if conditional automatically evaluates expressions, allowing omission of expression delimiters in that context but not everywhere.

Expressions beginning with ! must use expression delimiters or quoted/parenthesized escaping because ! is YAML-reserved; illustrated startsWith negation tests tag references. Source example is inert and not executed.
Expression evaluation requires specific syntax to distinguish it from a literal string; exact syntax and allowed positions depend on parent context rather than this standalone reminder.
